images.title: Each fold doubles the stack
images.purpose: Shows a folded sheet doubling its layers with every fold and asks whether 46 folds could reach the Moon.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Four small paper stacks in a row along the bottom left, growing in height, and a tall dotted arrow rising from the last stack to a small Moon at the top right.
images.exact_structure: Along the bottom left, four stacks of thin flat white rectangles with dark outlines, standing on one baseline and evenly spaced: the first has exactly 1 layer, the second 2 layers, the third 4 layers, the fourth 8 layers, all layers the same thickness. Under the stacks the numbers 1, 2, 4 and 8 in order. Above the row, one long thin amber (#E69F00) arrow running left to right over the stacks, labelled × 2 each fold. From the top of the 8 layer stack a dotted reddish purple (#CC79A7) arrow climbs steeply to the top right corner, where one plain grey (#6B7280) circle stands for the Moon, labelled Moon. Beside the dotted arrow, the label 46 folds? Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Every fold doubles the thickness, so the stack grows very fast.
